::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** April 18th 1899  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne  
**Manuscript:** MS Hampshire Record Office 9M55 F56/2
:::

My dear [Mrs Packe](people/person_1112.qmd)
I am sure that the correspondence would be most interesting and suggestive, only I am not quite sure in what way you thought of letting it appear, whether as the actual letters abridged or as a digest of them, or to shew a selection to anyone who might be writing an account of the times. [^1]  They would reflect the feeling of the early times surprisingly to many, and I think there would be surprise at how much the plain long services now so much despised were to people like them.[^2]

Perhaps if you liked to talk this over, you would let me know when you are coming to Crookham.  I should be very glad if you could spend a day or two here, as I now have room

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: With envelope addressed to Mrs Packe/Honies House/West Wickham/ Kent and postmarked Winchester 18 April 1899.
[^2]: The lifelong correspondence, now preserved in Hampshire Record Office, between [Anne Sturges Bourne](people/person_1379.qmd) (who had brought Penelope Packe up) and [Mary Anne Dyson](people/person_464.qmd).
[^3]: The ‘early times’ are those of the Tractarian revival.
